# Wholesale Vehicle Arbitration FAQs: What Dealers Need to Know


[Product + Tech](https://www.openlane.com/insights/category/product-tech/) |


- [Easy Mode](https://www.openlane.com/insights/tag/easy-mode/)


5 mins


Nov 18, 2026


Buying vehicles at wholesale auctions comes with a lot of decisions. And while finding the right inventory is the goal, it’s just as important to know what happens if a covered vehicle item doesn’t match its description.


That’s where wholesale vehicle arbitration comes in.


Whether you’re buying wholesale vehicles online for the first time or navigating auto auction arbitration, understanding your buyer protections and knowing how arbitration works can help you avoid surprises and make more confident purchases.


Here are answers to common questions about wholesale vehicle arbitration, including what OPENLANE covers and how to file a claim.


## What Is Wholesale Vehicle Arbitration?


Wholesale vehicle arbitration is a process that helps buyers resolve issues with vehicles purchased through wholesale auctions or online marketplaces.


If a vehicle has a covered item that wasn’t disclosed before the sale, the buyer may be able to file an arbitration claim. The marketplace then reviews the issue to determine whether it qualifies for a resolution under its arbitration policy.


For dealers buying vehicles online, arbitration is an important safeguard. It helps protect against certain unexpected repair costs on certain covered items and provides a way to address eligible issues after a purchase.


## How does OPENLANE approach arbitration?


OPENLANE’s arbitration policy is built around the needs of dealers buying vehicles digitally. Because buyers often rely on condition reports instead of inspecting vehicles in person, having clear information and reliable buyer protections matters.


OPENLANE combines[detailed vehicle condition reports](https://www.openlane.com/insights/what-youll-find-in-an-openlane-condition-report/) with arbitration coverage that goes beyond many standard wholesale auction policies. This includes protections for certain interior and technology features, as well as coverage for eligible lower-priced vehicles.


The goal is simple: help dealers know what they’re buying and give them a clear path forward if something isn’t as described.


## What Vehicle Issues Qualify for Arbitration?


Not every vehicle problem qualifies for arbitration. Coverage depends on the marketplace’s policy, the vehicle’s condition, what was disclosed before the sale, and the terms of the purchase.


Common types of issues that may qualify include undisclosed mechanical problems, structural damage, exterior damage and certain equipment failures.


## What does OPENLANE cover?


OPENLANE’s arbitration policy includes coverage for a range of mechanical, structural, exterior and interior issues on eligible vehicles.


One area where OPENLANE stands out is its expanded coverage for interior and technology features. Depending on the vehicle and its protection level, covered items may include:


- Power windows, locks and seats
- Panoramic roofs
- Backup cameras
- Air conditioning
- Navigation systems
- Radios


These may seem like smaller issues compared to major engine or structural problems, but repairs can add up quickly.


For example, a dealer who purchases a vehicle with an undisclosed backup camera issue may face an unexpected repair bill before the vehicle is ready to sell. With the right coverage, that issue may qualify for arbitration.


OPENLANE also doesn’t impose the same restrictive single-item repair-cost thresholds found in some other wholesale arbitration policies. That means a wider range of eligible issues can be considered without having to meet those types of minimum repair costs.


Coverage still depends on the vehicle, the issue and the applicable arbitration policy.


[Learn More About OPENLANE’s Arbitration Policy](https://www.openlane.com/insights/how-openlanes-arbitration-policy-enhances-buyer-protection/)


## Can You Arbitrate a Lower-Priced Wholesale Vehicle?


Yes, you can arbitrate a lower-priced wholesale vehicle, depending on the marketplace. Some wholesale auction policies limit arbitration coverage for lower-priced vehicles or vehicles with higher mileage.


That can be frustrating for dealers who regularly buy budget-friendly inventory, since even a lower-priced vehicle can come with unexpected repair costs.


OPENLANE offers certain arbitration protections on eligible vehicles priced under $6,000, rather than automatically excluding them based on price alone.


Coverage varies by vehicle value and sale terms, but this gives dealers sourcing lower-priced inventory an opportunity for protection that may not be available through other marketplaces.


## Are there Deadlines and Windows for Vehicle Arbitration Claims?


Timeframes for vehicle arbitration claims vary by marketplace. While some platforms allow only a brief window after purchase, others offer extended filing windows.


Because deadlines can be strict, it’s a good idea to inspect vehicles as soon as possible and report potential issues promptly.


OPENLANE’s As Described Guarantee generally provides a seven-day arbitration window from purchase for eligible claims.


With OPENLANE’s Extended Guarantee, eligible buyers may have seven days from delivery, with up to 14 days after purchase to open a claim, subject to the applicable terms.


## What Do You Need to File Successful Vehicle Arbitration Claims?


When submitting vehicle arbitration claims, dealerships generally need to clearly outline the issue and provide supporting documentation.


Helpful documentation may include photos of damage, videos of a malfunction, inspection reports or diagnostic information.


The more clearly you can show the problem, the easier it is for the arbitration team to understand what happened.


OPENLANE makes this part of the process easier with Mobile Arbitration.


Instead of taking photos on your phone, emailing them to yourself, and completing a claim later on your computer, you can upload everything directly through the OPENLANE app.


For example, if you discover undisclosed exterior damage while inspecting a newly delivered vehicle, you can photograph the issue and attach the images to your claim right away. You can also record videos of mechanical concerns or upload supporting documents from your mobile device.


## How Do You File an Arbitration Claim on OPENLANE?


Filing a wholesale vehicle arbitration claim doesn’t have to mean paperwork or switching between multiple devices.


With OPENLANE Mobile Arbitration, you can start and submit a claim directly from your phone.


Here’s how:


1. Open **Purchase History** in the OPENLANE app.
2. Select the vehicle you want to submit a claim for.
3. Tap **Start Vehicle Arbitration** .
4. Choose the reason for your claim.
5. Add details about the issue.
6. Upload photos, videos or supporting documents.
7. Review and submit your claim.


Once submitted, your claim goes to the OPENLANE Arbitration team for review.


You can complete the process while you’re inspecting the vehicle, whether you’re on the lot, in the service department, or elsewhere at your dealership.


Prefer using a computer? You can still submit arbitration claims through the OPENLANE website. Mobile Arbitration simply gives you another convenient option.


For a closer look, read[Easier Wholesale Vehicle Arbitration Has Arrived](https://www.openlane.com/insights/easier-wholesale-vehicle-arbitration-has-arrived/) .


## What Happens After You Submit an Arbitration Claim?


Once you submit a vehicle arbitration claim, the marketplace reviews the reported issue and any supporting documentation to determine whether it qualifies under the applicable policy. Depending on the claim, the arbitration team may need more information before deciding on next steps.


At OPENLANE, claims submitted through the website or[mobile app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/openlane-us/id1175036411) are sent to the Arbitration team for review.


If additional details are needed, the team will contact you. Including clear photos, videos and other relevant information with your initial submission can help limit unnecessary back-and-forth.


Mobile Arbitration doesn’t change the policy or how claims are reviewed. It simply makes it easier to get your information to the right team.


## Why Does Arbitration Matter When Buying Wholesale Vehicles Online?


When you’re buying vehicles online, you don’t always get to see them in person before making a purchase. That makes accurate condition reports and dependable buyer protections especially important.


A good arbitration policy for auto auction arbitration helps reduce the risk of unexpected costs and gives dealers a way to address eligible problems after the sale.


OPENLANE supports dealers with detailed condition reports, its As Described Guarantee on most inventory, expanded coverage for certain vehicle components, and convenient online and mobile claim submission.


Together, these protections and tools help make buying wholesale vehicles online more straightforward, so dealers can spend less time worrying about surprises and more time getting inventory ready to sell.


## Buy With More Confidence on OPENLANE


Understanding wholesale vehicle arbitration can help you make smarter buying decisions and avoid unnecessary surprises.


Before purchasing, take time to review the vehicle’s condition report, understand what protections apply and know your arbitration deadlines.


With OPENLANE, dealers have access to broad buyer protections and easy-to-use tools that make it simpler to report eligible issues when they come up.
